contract_changes.before: The linear span of \(\Lambda\) is all of \(\mathfrak q\). Otherwise the quotient linear map \(\mathfrak q\to\mathfrak q/\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\Lambda\) factors through the compact space \(Q=\mathfrak q/\Lambda\) and is onto a nonzero real vector space; that is impossible by [F4]. A discrete additive subgroup of a finite-dimensional real vector space that spans it is a lattice. To see this, a discrete subgroup has a neighborhood of zero containing no other subgroup point, so distinct subgroup points are uniformly separated and every bounded subset of it is finite. Choose a shortest nonzero vector \(\lambda_1\); the intersection with \(\mathbb R\lambda_1\) is \(\mathbb Z\lambda_1\), since any smaller positive step would contradict shortestness. If projections of subgroup points to \(\lambda_1^\perp\) approach zero, subtract nearest integer multiples of \(\lambda_1\); the resulting points lie in a bounded set, hence in a finite set, so zero is isolated in the projected subgroup. The projection remains discrete and spans \(\lambda_1^\perp\). Induction on \(d\) gives a lattice basis for the projection; lifting that finite basis and adjoining \(\lambda_1\) gives a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\) of \(\Lambda\) that is also a real basis of \(\mathfrak q\). [F4, step 1.2, algebra]

contract_changes.before: Define the nonzero real linear functional \(\ell:\mathfrak q\to\mathbb R\) by \(\ell(\lambda_1)=1\) and \(\ell(\lambda_j)=0\) for \(2\leq j\leq d\). Then \(\ell(\Lambda)\subseteq\mathbb Z\). Define \(\chi_Q(\exp_Q X):=\exp(2\pi i\,\ell(X))\). This is well defined because two logarithms differ by an element of \(\Lambda\). It is a homomorphism by additivity of both the exponential map on the abelian Lie algebra and \(\ell\); it is smooth because the exponential map is a local diffeomorphism near zero and its translates are local diffeomorphisms everywhere. It is nontrivial: \(\exp_Q(\lambda_1/2)\ne e\), while \(\chi_Q(\exp_Q(\lambda_1/2))=-1\). [F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]
